title: OSHA penalties 2026: current maximum fines per violation
seoTitle: OSHA penalties 2026: maximum fines per violation
description: OSHA's current maximum penalties for 2026: serious, other-than-serious, failure to abate, willful and repeated violations, from OSHA's own figures.
summary: OSHA's maximum penalty is $16,550 per serious or other-than-serious violation and $165,514 per willful or repeated violation, for penalties assessed after Jan. 15, 2026.
coverPrompt: A tidy workplace safety office with binders, a hard hat and safety glasses on a desk beside a window, soft daylight, no screens, no text, no people

sections.heading: How do maximum penalties apply in state-plan states?
sections.opening: States that run their own OSHA-approved plans must adopt maximum penalties at least as effective as federal OSHA's, and state plans don't have to fine state and local government employers.

sections.heading: How much does OSHA propose in practice?
sections.opening: Across 459,547 citations of 29 CFR standards in FY2022–FY2026, the median initial penalty for a citation with a penalty was $3,972, and the middle half ran from $2,000 to $6,620; penalties can be reduced on settlement or after a contest.

sections.heading: Where do the amounts come from?
sections.opening: OSHA adjusts its maximum penalties for inflation every January; the amounts above apply to penalties assessed after Jan. 15, 2026, as published on OSHA's penalties page.

method: Maximum amounts copied from OSHA's penalties page on the date shown; enforcement figures from the U.S. Department of Labor OSHA violation dataset.
